analyzed_vuln.description: `htmlParseDocument` invokes the SAX `endDocument` callback unconditionally whenever the callback pointer is present, unlike `startDocument` and normal SAX events which also require `!ctxt->disableSAX`. In this PoV, allocation failure during parsing/encoding handling leaves the context in the fatal OOM/EOF state with `disableSAX == 1` and may halt the parser, freeing its input buffer and replacing input cursors with the static empty-string sentinel. The function nevertheless calls `endDocument` at line 5057. The default SAX2 callback then consumes encoding/input metadata from this aborted context, resulting in the observed one-byte read beyond global sentinel storage. The root cause is the missing failed/disabled-parser guard at the end-document dispatch, not the callback itself.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The HTML fuzz harness interprets the first four PoC bytes as parser options and the next four as an allocation-failure selector; for this 46-byte PoC, the selector `0x2d380180 % 47` yields `maxAlloc = 25`. The remaining document is `<style>\xffhttp-equivcontentcharset=TSCII`. The non-ASCII byte activates HTML encoding discovery, which finds the trailing `TSCII` charset and enters encoding conversion/allocation paths. The injected failure places the parser in OOM/EOF state and sets `disableSAX`, but the pull parser continues to the unconditional `endDocument` dispatch. Triggering requires a successfully created parser/SAX handler, a later fatal allocation failure that disables SAX, and state such as this encoding-switching input that leaves end-document processing unsafe.

patch_result.patch:
--- a/HTMLparser.c
+++ b/HTMLparser.c
@@ -5053,7 +5053,8 @@
     /*
      * SAX: end of the document processing.
      */
-    if ((ctxt->sax) && (ctxt->sax->endDocument != NULL))
+    if ((ctxt->sax) && (ctxt->sax->endDocument != NULL) &&
+	(!ctxt->disableSAX))
         ctxt->sax->endDocument(ctxt->userData);
 
     if ((!(ctxt->options & HTML_PARSE_NODEFDTD)) && (ctxt->myDoc != NULL)) {

args: In libxml2/HTMLparser.c, analyze all endDocument callback dispatches in htmlParseDocument (around lines 4956-5057), htmlParseTryOrFinish (around lines 5572, 5790, and 6237), and htmlParseChunk (around line 6325). Which dispatches can occur after fatal errors set ctxt->disableSAX, and what minimal root-cause fix is consistent with the parser's SAX dispatch policy? Also note whether skipping endDocument when disableSAX is set could disrupt parser state transitions.

The reported PoV causes an allocation failure during encoding conversion in pull parsing. htmlParseDocument begins with a guarded startDocument callback, but its final endDocument callback checks only ctxt->sax and the callback pointer. The OOM path sets ctxt->disableSAX=1, input cursors may point to an empty global sentinel, and default SAX2 endDocument accesses unsafe aborted-context metadata, producing a global-buffer-overflow at line 5057. I suspect the direct fix is adding !ctxt->disableSAX to the final callback guard, but I am checking analogous push-parser dispatches to ensure the root policy is applied correctly and no state update depends on the callback.
